safety.disclaimer: This is general advice, not medical advice. Staff at the blood bank make the final decision.
safety.n1: You have a fever, cold or infection
safety.n2: You donated whole blood in the last 3 to 4 months
safety.n3: You had surgery, a tattoo or piercing recently
safety.n5: You take medicines that your doctor says affect donation
safety.r1t: Blood donation is voluntary. If someone asks for money, do not continue and report the profile.
safety.r2: Meet at a hospital or blood bank
safety.r2t: Donate only at a medical facility. Avoid meeting in private places.
safety.r3t: Call the hospital to check the patient and blood group before you travel.
safety.r4t: Give your phone number to the requester only. Never share bank or card details.
safety.subtitle: Simple rules that keep donors and patients safe.
safety.title: Safety and advisory

tips.a1: Rest for 10 to 15 minutes and have a snack and a drink before leaving.
tips.a2: Drink more fluids than usual for the next day.
tips.a3: Skip heavy lifting and hard exercise for the rest of the day.
tips.a4: Keep the bandage on for several hours. Lie down if you feel faint.
tips.b1: Drink an extra 500 ml of water in the hour before you donate.
tips.b2: Eat a normal meal with iron-rich food such as meat, lentils or spinach.
tips.b3: Sleep well the night before and avoid alcohol for 24 hours.
tips.b4: Carry a valid ID and a list of any medicines you take.
tips.d1: A whole-blood donation itself takes around 10 minutes.
tips.d2: Relax, breathe normally and look away if needles bother you.
tips.d3: Tell the staff at once if you feel dizzy, cold or unwell.
tips.d4: Keep your arm still and squeeze the ball if you’re asked to.
tips.subtitle: What to do before, during and after you donate.
tips.title: Blood donation tips and guidelines

about.manifesto: Blood donation isn't a transaction. It's a quiet promise between strangers — and we're here to make keeping it feel effortless.
about.intro: Blood Connect is a community-focused blood donation initiative that connects voluntary blood donors with people who need blood. Our goal is to make blood donation coordination more accessible, organized, and reliable.
about.whoText1: Finding a blood donor during an emergency can be stressful and time-sensitive. Blood Connect aims to simplify that process by creating a structured platform where people can find available donors and volunteers can coordinate blood requests.
about.whoText2: We are starting our operations in Tangail, Bangladesh, with a vision to expand our support to more communities across the country.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.text: To connect voluntary blood donors with people in need through an organized, accessible, and responsible coordination system supported by dedicated volunteers.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.text: To create a world where everyone has access to timely and reliable blood donation support, fostering a culture of generosity and community care.

about.valuesText: The principles that guide how we serve our community.

humanity.title: Humanity First
humanity.text: We believe every person deserves access to timely blood donation support, regardless of their background.

trust.title: Trust & Transparency
trust.text: We work to verify blood requests and coordinate responsibly to build a reliable donation community.

community.title: Community Driven
community.text: We bring donors, volunteers, and people in need together to make a meaningful difference.

service.title: Responsible Service
service.text: We respect donor privacy, voluntary participation, and the importance of responsible coordination.

about.ctaText: Your willingness to donate blood can make a real difference. Join our community and help someone find hope.
